# Recurrence ledger

Finding-level tracking, one row per defect an adopter reported. The README tracks **plans**;
findings recur **across** plans, which plan granularity structurally cannot see.

## The rule

> **A finding may not be marked closed without naming a guard that exists.**

"Fixed in source" is not a closure. A fix with nothing holding it in place is precisely what
produced twelve reports of the same handful of defects. If no guard can express the
invariant, the finding stays **open** with a note saying why, and every subsequent plan lists
it.

`scripts/checks/recurrence.test.ts` enforces this: a `closed` row whose guard is missing,
empty, or does not resolve to a real npm script or file fails CI. It also fails when a
`feedback-*.md` report exists that no row references — a new report must be triaged into
this table, not just filed.

## Closed — awaiting release — 16

Fixed on `main` with a guard, and **not yet reachable by `pnpm add`**. An adopter who
tests today still meets every one of these. This section exists because on 2026-08-08 two
adopters re-hit four findings the ledger listed as closed: they had been merged and
unpublished for four days, and `Closed — 0 open` said nothing about that. Draining this
table is a release, not a fix.

| Finding | Reports | Mech. | Guard | How it holds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AppShell content sits flush; every adopter writes the same wrapper | 2 (08-08, 08-08) | A | `computed:check` | Reported three times (07-24, 08-06, 08-08). Documenting it was chosen twice and re-reported twice, so `padding` now DEFAULTS to space step 6 with `none` as the opt-out. The CLI's generated dashboard drops the inline style it used to model the workaround with — the very thing its sibling AGENTS.md forbids. |
| Findings closed in the ledger are unreachable by `pnpm add` for days | 2 (08-08, 08-08) | G | `recurrence:shipped` | The ledger read `Open — 0` while two adopters re-hit four closed findings. Verified from npm rather than assumed: 0.16.1 and CLI 0.7.2 carry the 08-06 fixes and were published 2026-08-10T05:09Z, two days AFTER both reports, which tested the newest version that existed. Rows now carry `shippedIn`, RECURRENCE.md separates "awaiting release" from "shipped", and recurrence:shipped compares the two against the npm registry. |
| An icon composed next to a label inside a Button renders touching | 1 (08-08) | A | `computed:check` | All children go into ONE inner span, so the button's flex `gap` applied between the loading Spinner and that wrapper and never between an icon and its label. The wrapper is now a flex row inheriting the gap, so composing an icon with a label needs no adopter CSS — which also removes the reason to write layout CSS against the undocumented `> span`. |
| Card is not `position: relative`; a stretched link covers the viewport | 1 (08-08) | A | `computed:check` | The stretched-link idiom is what every dashboard project grid uses. Without a containing block the ::after overlay resolved against the viewport and swallowed every click in the app, silently — found only because a Playwright click timed out. The probe hit-tests a button outside the card. |
| 37 npm-shipped registry entries have never been props-parity checked | 1 (08-08) | F | `meta:check` | props-parity and typedefs-parity resolved source through registry files[], which is empty for npm-shipped packages, so both hit `if (tsx.length === 0) continue`. Every chart, flow node and editor was unchecked for the life of the guard — which is why AreaChart.format was real, documented in TSDoc, and invisible to registry.json/llms.txt. Turning it on surfaced 39 undocumented props and 114 missing typeDefs. A per-prefix coverage floor now fails loudly if an entry drops back out. |
| Checkbox's decoration intercepts pointer events, breaking .check() | 1 (08-08) | A | `computed:check` | The real input is visually hidden beneath the decoration, so every getByRole(checkbox).check() in every adopter suite failed with "intercepts pointer events" and needed { force: true }. Real users click the label and never notice, which is why it survived. The probe hit-tests the control centre. |
| Fields in a Grid row put their inputs at different heights | 1 (08-08) | E | `computed:check` | Reproduced at 13.6px, but not for the reported reason: Field renders label -> control -> description, so the description sits BELOW the input and cannot push it down. The cause was .field being a grid with the default align-content: stretch, so as a cell in a taller row its rows absorbed the slack and a three-row field distributed it differently from a two-row one. align-content: start pins them to their natural sizes. |

Making it a grid container stretches the child by default, which is what an adopter already expects from the row. Reported as "Grid's align prop didn't fix it" — correctly, because the item was never the element failing to stretch. |

SideNavItem, ShellHeaderNavLink and four others gained `id` in an earlier sweep; Switcher was missed. The guard asserts each link-shaped type declares it AND that the component keys on it rather than merely declaring it. |

The contract is published in AI-RULES.md, llms.txt and CLAUDE.md. |

| `cascivo create`'s ESLint config inspects zero TypeScript files | 1 (08-08) | F | `scaffold:check` | scaffold-contract had a test named "pre-wires the react-hooks/immutability escape so lint passes on a fresh app" that string-matched the config text and passed the whole time. The template registered no TS parser and no `files` pattern, so ESLint 9 skipped every .ts/.tsx. scaffold-lint now runs the REAL ESLint over an app generated by the REAL built CLI and asserts the file count it reported on equals the number of TypeScript files generated, plus a control case (an unused local must error) so the immutability assertion cannot be satisfied by a config that lints nothing. |
| Sub-day time domains render a single date tick | 1 (08-08) | B | `packages/charts/src/engine/scale-time.test.ts` | pickInterval had one entry per unit and took the first that fit, accepting a 1-tick undershoot over 23 ticks. Replaced with a step ladder choosing the candidate closest to the requested count in log space. A second, independent defect surfaced while fixing it: TimeScale.tickFormat() was dead code called by nothing, so every time axis fell through to toLocaleDateString() and would have rendered the same date on each tick even with correct ticks. |
| Generated index.html emits unlayered CSS | 1 (08-08) | D | `unlayered:check` | unlayered:check globbed packages/**/src/**/*.css, so the one template every adopter starts from was exempt from the rule it teaches — its sibling AGENTS.md says "never emit it". The guard now parses <style> blocks inside packages/cli/src/commands/*.ts. |
| DataTable zebra striping paints rows the colour they already are | 1 (08-08) | E | `computed:check` | Reported as "no visible effect in the dark theme"; it was worse and not theme-specific. Every theme aliases --cascivo-color-bg-subtle straight to --cascivo-color-surface, so striping a table that sits on a surface — a table in a Card, the normal composition — was a no-op with measured ΔL of exactly 0.0000 in all three themes. Replaced with a translucent foreground overlay that darkens on light themes and lightens on dark. Only observable in a browser: the declaration looks correct in source, and the first replacement named a token that does not exist, which computes to transparent and is indistinguishable from the original bug except by measuring painted alpha. |

## Mechanisms

Defined in [`README.md`](README.md). Briefly: **A** a claim that exists only as prose ·
**B** a fact hand-authored instead of derived from source · **C** one fact with several
owners · **D** a fix that landed on one surface only · **E** only observable in a
consumer-shaped environment · **F** the guard re-implements the adopter's tool instead of
running it · **G** closed on `main`, absent from the registry the adopter installs.
